parties:
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and public Works, Bangladesh Secretariat, Ramna, Dhaka ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Mohammad Alam and another ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 6. High Court Division examined two witnesses and made the rule absolute as if it were trying a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. We have mentioned the dates which were fixed for hearing of the case in the Court of Settlement. Those dates apparently show that the writ petitioner repeatedly prayed time for hearing but he failed to prove the case by filing legal documents of title. The Court of Settlement finding no other alternative took up the case for hearing on 22.05.2001, but on that day also the respondent did not take any step. The court adjourned the matter for ends of justice. On two subsequent dates on 24.06.2001 and 27.07.2001 also the respondent did not take any step. Ultimately the court took up the case for disposal on 30.09.2001. The Court observed that on repeated occasions the respondent did not even appear and drag the matter for indefinite period; that on 13.3.2001 the matter was adjourned for the last time on his on his prayer; and the case was adjourned to 11.4.2001 for hearing; that despite that on two successive dated the matter was adjourned on his prayer; that thereafter the respondent did not take any step in the case and that from his conduct it was apparent that he was not interested to prosecute the matter. It further observed that the respondent filed some photo copies of applications and papers, but he did not file the original petitions and the documents and that he failed to prove the case on merit.
